the power properties of repeated measures and multivariate models vary significantly across main effects and interaction effects and that the power differences between these 2 methods are also significantly influenced by the covariance structures.

the power properties of hierarchical multivariate linear model for main effects and interaction effects in the balanced design, which is the first study to compare the traditional repeated measures and the hierarchical multivariate linear modeling in the balanced design in the literature.

the power properties of hierarchical multivariate linear model and repeated measures analysis of variance for longitudinal studies in a balanced full-crossed design.

the traditional repeated measures and the hierarchical multivariate linear model should be used in combination to achieve the most efficient power in longitudinal studies.
the traditional repeated measures model should be used for the main effects in the longitudinal studies, but the hierarchical multivariate linear model should be used in the interaction effects.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the traditional repeated measures model has the highest power for the main effects and the hierarchical multivariate linear model has the highest for the interaction effects.

hierarchical multivariate linear modeling is a more powerful method than traditional repeated measures for interaction effects, whereas traditional repeated measures are more powerful than hierarchical multivariate linear methods for main effects.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of statistical model for the analysis of longitudinal data is important and should not be based on tradition or convenience alone.
traditional repeated measures should be used when the primary focus of the study is on main effects and the hierarchical multivariate linear model when the primary focus is on interaction effects.
researchers need to be careful when selecting the statistical model to be applied to the data.
